title: What is known about 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_1LC0LD_1RA1LF_---1LD_1LD1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_1LC0LD_1RA1LF_---1LD_1LD1LB.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine was one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project; an outside Rocq proof has since shown that it halts when started on a blank tape, after about 3.1×10957 steps. Its run is a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k rewrites the word to the right of the block by applying one fixed map P to it exactly 2k times. P is a single trip of the head into the word and back. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it halts. Busycoq pull request 94 (Alex Havrilla of DeepMind, 2026-11-17) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: it uses no axioms (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. By their count it halts after about 3.1×10957 steps. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open.

What this repository found on its own. The clock is proved in Lean for every k and every word: if P takes the word through 2k trips, the tick happens, in an exactly known number of steps. What P does over many trips, and what happens at the end of a phase, was not proved here. An exact accelerated simulator, checked against the direct one at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, follows the run through 10 phases to 8.229·1069 steps without a halt. The halt the proof finds comes much later.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 137 cells have been visited and 66 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: The self-loops of the table cross runs of any length: sweep_A1, sweep_C0, for every length and every tape around.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is E on 0. E is entered only from B on 1 (0LE), and B from A on 0 (1RB, after which E reads the 1 that A just wrote, so no halt) or from F on 1 (1LB): the machine halts exactly when F reads a 1 with 0 1 to its left, 0 1 F>1. Both directions are proved in Lean, by a case split on the cells the head reads: a configuration halts two steps later if and only if it is 0 1 F>1 (halt_iff_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: The sweep and the merge
claims.text: rule_sweep: 0 0 D> 1^(2+2n) 0 becomes 1 0^(3+2n) 1 B> (the block is swept into 0s); rule_merge: 1 0 D> 1 becomes D> 1 1 1, for every n and all tapes around.

claims.title: The clock, for every k
claims.text: tick: for every k, every word W and all tapes L, if W reaches W' by 2k P-steps (each one an excursion L 0^2 1 B> W → L D> 1^2 0 W') of total cost E, then L 0 0 D> 1^(2+2k) 0 W reaches L D> 1^(2+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 11·2k − 2 steps. Strong induction on k: the tick is the sweep, one P-step, ticks 0 … k−1, and the merge. tick_left_end: the same at the left end of the tape.

claims.title: The exact accelerated run
claims.text: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py simulates cell by cell, but does a tick at once when its 2k P-steps all come back (the theorem above; P computed by running the machine, P2k memoized on the part of the word it reads). It gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, and follows the run through 10 phases to 8.229·1069 steps: no halt.

claims.title: What the word does
claims.text: The word is a string of the blocks 1 and 1^3 separated by single 0s. P rewrites a front part of variable length; the words do not repeat with a period 2j (so the doubling memo is slow here and the banded memo is used), unlike the other four machines. It behaves like a counter in a non-binary numeration; not identified. Every phase measured ends at the same kind of word: 1 1 3 3 … 3 1 followed by a double 0 (in the phases with last blocks 1^54, 1^94, …, 1^454, the run of 3s has 20 to 30 blocks); the last blocks of the phases grow by a factor of about 1.7 from one phase to the next (8, 18, 30, 54, 94, 158, 268, 454).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape? (this repository’s own ledger)
claims.text: Not decided by the results on this page alone. It is decided outside: busycoq pull request 94 proves that it halts (see the verdict). Before the proof: A normal tick cannot halt (the clock theorem). Halting needs a P-step that does not come back — that happens only at the end of a phase — followed by F on a 1 with 0 1 to its left (0 1 F>1). Open here: what P does over 2k trips (a counter in the word), what a phase end builds, and whether one ever reaches the halting configuration.

check: ./tmrun 1RB0RA_0RC0LE_1LC0LD_1RA1LF_---1LD_1LD1LB 20000000000 at F L 1500     # the visits of the left end

explainer.lede: It halts, after about 3.1×10<sup>957</sup> steps. Its run is a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k makes 2<sup>k</sup> trips of the head into the word beside the block. The proof replays the whole run with a fast simulator that jumps over long series of trips using a table it builds and checks, until the head reads a 0 in state E, which has no transition.

facts.text: Whenever its 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return, tick k = 2<sup>k</sup> trips P of the head into the word, in E + 11·2<sup>k</sup> − 2 steps.
No halt, in an exact accelerated run through 10 phases.
The only way it can stop (proved in Lean). A normal tick never gets there, so the halt the proof finds comes at the end of a phase.

sections.heading: A checked table of counter runs, and one long exact replay
html: The proof is busycoq pull request 94 by Alex Havrilla of DeepMind. We compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1, and it uses no axioms: even its big-number arithmetic is built from scratch, with digits in base 64, rather than with Coq's machine integers.

How the proof writes the tape. The proof stores the tape as runs. Right of the clock block lies the word, a list of tokens 0 1^(2u+1): a 0 followed by an odd run of 1s. The blocks 1 and 1^3 in which this repository wrote the word are the tokens with u = 0 and u = 1, that is 01 and 0111. On the left, long stretches are stored as runs or as one binary number. One trip of the head into the word and back (the map P) is proved to act on the token list by an explicit rule.

The table. Most of the time goes into long series of trips over a front of the word made only of 01 and 0111. Such a front behaves like a counter. With x tokens 01 and y tokens 0111 its width is W = x + 2y, and repeating the trip runs the counter down until it is used up. What is left at the end, and after how many trips, depends only on W and y. The proof builds a table of these outcomes for every width W from 4 to 4,583 and every y up to W/2. It fills each row from the rows before it (a dynamic program) and checks every row as it goes, so the table itself is part of the proof. A second, smaller table does the same for a run of k tokens 0111. This fits what this repository saw: every phase ended at a word 1 1 3 3 … 3 1, a long run of 0111.

The replay. With the tables in hand, the computer replays the run from the blank tape in 604,910 fused macro steps. In 32,833 of them a whole counter run is skipped by looking it up in the table. The counts involved grow to about 3,180 bits. The last step lands on state E reading a 0, which has no transition, so the machine halts. The number of machine steps, about 3.123449×10957, is added up along the way.

What is proved and what is computed. Short pieces of the run (sweeps over runs, bounces and the trip P) are proved for every length. Theorems say that every row of either table is a true statement about the machine, and that each fused macro step, a table lookup included, is a true piece of its run. The computer then checks with Coq's vm_compute that building the tables succeeds and that the replay ends in the halting configuration.

sections.heading: A block that grows by two, each tick twice as long
html: Watch the tape each time the head, in state F, sits at the left end. It always reads F>0 1^L 0 W: a block of L ones, then a word W of short blocks. Within a phase L grows by 2 per visit and each visit takes about twice as long as the one before. From the real run:

Inside one tick the machine runs a recursion. The head sweeps the block into 0s, makes one trip into the word W (a P-step: it rewrites the front of W and comes back), and then performs ticks 0, 1, …, k−1 on a new small block, each one eating two of the 0s it left; finally it merges. So tick k contains one P-step plus ticks 0 … k−1: 1 + 1 + 2 + … + 2k−1 = 2k P-steps in all. The word sees nothing but P, applied 2k times.

This is proved in Lean for every k and every word (tick in lean/Clock.lean): if 2k P-steps of total cost E take W to W', then 0 0 D> 1^(2+2k) 0 W reaches D> 1^(2+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 11·2k − 2 steps.

sections.heading: What P does to the word
html: The word is a string of the two blocks 1 (written .) and 1^3 (written #) separated by single 0s. From the visit at step 25,712, one P-step per line:

Each P-step rewrites a front part of the word, of varying length; the far end changes rarely. Unlike the four other machines of the family the words do not come back with a period 2j, so the counter hidden in the word is not a plain binary one. It was not identified here; the proof handles it with a table of counter runs (first section).

What ends a phase is the same each time: the trip that fails meets a word 1 1 3 3 … 3 1 followed by a double 0 — a run of 20 to 30 blocks 3 in the long phases — as if a counter whose digits are 1 and 3 had reached its last value. The last block of a phase grows by a factor of about 1.7 from one phase to the next: 1^8, 1^18, 1^30, 1^54, 1^94, 1^158, 1^268, 1^454.

sections.heading: A phase ends when a trip does not come back
html: The tick needs every one of its 2k trips to come back to the block. When one does not (the front of the word has run out), the clock breaks: the head goes on to the left over the half-built recursion, the block is dissolved into the word, and a new phase starts from a short block. sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is E on 0. E is entered only from B on 1 (0LE), and B from A on 0 (1RB, after which E reads the 1 that A just wrote, so no halt) or from F on 1 (1LB): the machine halts exactly when F reads a 1 with 0 1 to its left, 0 1 F>1.

A normal tick never halts: the Lean theorem says it reaches its end. So a halt can only come at the end of a phase, in the trip that does not come back or in what follows it before the next visit of the left end. The accelerated run simulates exactly those parts cell by cell, and none of the 10 phase ends halted. Whether a later one does depends on the word the earlier phases built, which looks irregular. The outside proof settles it: the run halts at a much later point, after about 3.1×10957 steps.

family: clock and word map (block grows by 2, the word is rewritten by 2^k excursions)
summary: A clock: at each visit of the left end in state F the block 1^(2+2k) has grown by 2, and the word to its right has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one excursion of the head into the word) — proved in Lean for every k, for each tick whose 2^k trips all return; a phase ends when P fails to come back. Exact accelerated run: 10 phases to 8.229·10<sup>69</sup> steps, no halt. Halting needs F on a 1 with 0 1 to its left (0 1 F>1). Decided outside: busycoq PR 94 proves in Rocq that it halts (compiled here).
